How do you normally start the conversation, how do you avoid silent pauses?
What are your go to questions or topics when speaking to someone new?

Round here its all about the weather then where your from what you do just small talk. Pauses will happen its not the end of the world be interested in what the other person is saying and ask a follow up question.
I frequently start off with, "what do you do for fun?" When driving a person somewhere is awkward to not talk, so I like to ask them about themselves.
"Hey whats up?" and go from there. Act interested in what they have to say and ask relevant questions.

I like to keep it light by finding out their religious and political backgrounds. After that it's mostly light feminism and socioeconomic inequalities amongst minorities and women. Oh and baking, I also love baking.

I talk a lot. So I just talk until something comes up and we can converse. I really like to ask the question "If a zombie apocalypse were to begin right now and you could only save two people who would they be?" You can ask why if you want, but the second part to the question is "Now they are both being attacked by zombies and you can only save one. Who do you choose?" You can learn a lot and stem other conversations from there.

Depends on circumstance. How do I know this person. A vast majority of people love sports, so that's a pretty good topic. Am I more familiar with you? Maybe talk about movies or video games. Basically, just have a bunch of topics you're interested in and then talk about whatever interests intersect. I do reiterate though, for the public at large, sports is the safest bet. Movies and tv comes in a close second, but there's too much variety to watch.

I live in a tourist destination type town, and the people that do live here generally aren't here longer than 6 months to a year - just seasonal work, that sort of stuff. So I find I can get away with "how are you / where are you from / have you been here long / what are you're plans after here" and then kind of just take it from there. On the one hand its useful having a standard set of questions that you can fall back on and will generally see you right. On the other, it gets pretty tedious having essentially the same conversation with every new person you meet - if I'm not the one asking the questions, then they probably are.
Religion, abortion, politics, and economics are my go to topics when meeting someone new.
What are your passions? What are you working towards? Truthfully, how are you doing?
